title: Memorial Day, the launch
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Memorial Day. The launch full of trailers and out-of-town boats. The uncle charges nothing for the ramp and never has. Gully directs traffic with a crab pot lid. Wood draws the lid. The uncle watches the boats go out and counts them back.

panels.composition: The boat launch on a holiday: trailers backed down, boats going in, out-of-town trucks. GULLY waving a crab pot lid like a flag. The UNCLE on his pot. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a crowded boat launch on a holiday with trailers backing boats into the water, a stocky teenager waving a crab pot lid to direct them, an old man seated on a crab pot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The lid. Gully's hand. A flag the strip draws better than any flag.

image.prompt: close on a teenager's hand holding up a round crab pot lid like a signal flag, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The uncle counting boats out with his fingers. Nine.

image.prompt: an old man on a crab pot counting on his fingers as boats head out onto a bay, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Dusk. Boats coming back. The uncle counting. Nine. His fingers going down. He doesn't get up till the ninth. The strip stays till the ninth too.

image.prompt: a boat launch at dusk with boats returning while an old man counts them in on his fingers, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Nine out, nine back. The uncle doesn't get up till the ninth.
